summary: Kilinti, the ents and the forest peoples: the Great Moot, the clearings, the waking groves and the charter that asks only for timber.

slow_counsel.name: Slow Counsel
slow_counsel.desc: A question raised in the thaw is answered at the harvest, and the answer holds.

slow_counsel_2.name: A Moot of Seasons
slow_counsel_2.desc: The Moot meets at each turning of the year, and no matter is ever left half-finished.

forest_villages.name: Clearings and Villages
forest_villages.desc: Walled villages in the clearings, sown fields beneath the trees.

forest_villages_2.name: The People of the Eaves
forest_villages_2.desc: The forest peoples grow in number beneath the eaves, nearly the ents' kin.

forest_rangers.name: Rangers of the Deep Woods
forest_rangers.desc: Rangers who walk where the ents walk, and leave no track.

secret_paths.name: Paths Only We Know
secret_paths.desc: A host that enters Kilinti without a guide does not come out.

slow_march.name: The Slow March
slow_march.desc: The groves march at the pace of a seedling, and arrive when they mean to.

slow_march_2.name: The Forest Stands
slow_march_2.desc: The forest stands as one, trunk by trunk and root by root.

scholars_in_the_woods.name: Scholars Among the Trees
scholars_in_the_woods.desc: Scholars sit at the roots and listen; the ents teach them one thing a year.

woods_awake.name: The Woods Awake
woods_awake.desc: The Great Moot has answered, and the groves are awake.

groves_march.name: The Groves March
groves_march.desc: Root from soil, the groves walk to the border.

forest_heals.name: The Forest Heals
forest_heals.desc: Saplings spring up where the burning was, and the ents walk slowly home.

the_burning_remembered.title: The Burning Remembered
the_burning_remembered.desc: The eldest ents speak, slowly, of forests that burned in an age of the dead, and of how the burning ended and the woods grew back. It is not a lament. It is a reminder that what is cut may be grown, in time.

pilgrims_at_the_forest_edge.title: Pilgrims at the Forest Edge
pilgrims_at_the_forest_edge.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer have come to the villages beneath the eaves, with bread, linen and a plan for a hospital. The ents watch from the trees. The forest peoples ask the Moot whether to let them stay.

options.name: Let the almoners tend the villages.

the_timber_buyers.title: The Timber-Buyers
the_timber_buyers.desc: The Golden Court's timber-buyers have arrived with a contract for the oldest groves and a purse of silver heavy enough to be noticed. The Moot may sell the young wood, or refuse the old trees entirely.

refugees_under_the_eaves.title: Refugees Under the Eaves
refugees_under_the_eaves.desc: Villagers from the burning lands have fled into the forest, thin and silent. The ents let them pass beneath the boughs, and the forest peoples ask whether to take them in or guide them out the other side.

focuses.name: The Great Moot
focuses.desc: The ents of the old woods speak slowly. A question raised in the thaw is answered at the harvest, if at all, and the answer is generally that it was a good question.

focuses.name: Voices of the Old Trees
focuses.desc: The eldest trees are heard before the youngest, and the youngest are heard before the saplings. The Moot begins with a silence that may last a day.

focuses.name: The Burning Remembered
focuses.desc: The ents remember the forests of the Third Age burning and growing back. The memory is not bitter; it is patient, and it shapes every decision they make.

focuses.name: A Moot of Seasons
focuses.desc: The Moot is held four times a year, at the turning of the seasons, and each time it takes up exactly what it set down the time before. Nothing is ever left unfinished and nothing is ever hurried.

focuses.name: Oaths Older Than Crowns
focuses.desc: The ents swore to guard the forest long before there was a crown to guard it for. Their oath to the Concord is a younger and lesser thing, kept faithfully, in its place.

focuses.name: The Hush of the Forest
focuses.desc: Pilgrims walk at the forest's edge, speaking quietly, as one does in a place older than speech. The ents watch them go by and say nothing for a season.

focuses.name: The Moot Decides
focuses.desc: After a year and a day, the Great Moot gives its answer. The answer is short, and everyone present has already known it for months.

focuses.name: The Forest Peoples
focuses.desc: Beneath the old trees live the forest peoples, woodcutters, hunters and herders of the clearings. They speak for Kilinti where the ents cannot be hurried.

focuses.name: Woodsmen and Charcoal
focuses.desc: Charcoal-burners and woodsmen set up their camps in the fallen timber. Nothing that stands is cut, and nothing that has fallen is wasted.

focuses.name: Clearings and Villages
focuses.desc: The clearings are sown, the villages are walled and the paths between them are cleared of brush. The ents stand at the edge of each, and nobody has ever asked them to go.

focuses.name: Bows of the Clearings
focuses.desc: The hunters of the clearings are taught to draw together, loose together and fall back together. They fight best from the trees, and so they do.

focuses.name: Rangers of the Deep Woods
focuses.desc: The rangers of the deep woods walk where the ents walk. They sleep in the roots of the oldest trees and travel without leaving a track.

focuses.name: The Timber-Buyers
focuses.desc: The Golden Court's timber-buyers want the oldest trees, and have the contracts to prove it. The Moot has not agreed to sell, and is in no hurry to disagree.

focuses.name: The People of the Eaves
focuses.desc: The forest peoples grow in number under the eaves, and no one now speaks of leaving. They are the ents' neighbours, and nearly their kin.

focuses.name: Wake the Groves
focuses.desc: The groves of Kilinti are older than the Concord, older than the Wall and older than any living memory. When the Moot decides, they wake, and not before.

focuses.name: Grove Wardings
focuses.desc: The ents sing the old wardings, low and slow, and the trees answer. Few men can hear it, and none who have heard it forget.

focuses.name: Paths Only We Know
focuses.desc: The forest peoples share with the ents the paths no stranger has ever found. A host that enters Kilinti without a guide will not come out.

focuses.name: The Slow March
focuses.desc: The groves can march, if they are asked, and if the ask is courteous. They go at the pace of a seedling and arrive when they mean to.

focuses.name: Rooted Defence
focuses.desc: The forest peoples build their forts in the roots of the oldest trees, and the ents lean in to help. The result is a wall no ram can take.

focuses.name: Grove Hosts
focuses.desc: The groves are organised into hosts of their own, led by an ent and followed by a company of forest peoples. They do not march far, but they do not move back either.

focuses.name: The Forest Stands
focuses.desc: The forest of Kilinti stands as one, trunk by trunk and root by root. It will not advance, and it will not yield.

focuses.name: The Old Charter
focuses.desc: The Charters of Parim ask very little of Kilinti: timber and the occasional courtesy. The ents have kept the bargain for centuries, and see no reason to stop.

focuses.name: Timber for the Crown
focuses.desc: The forest peoples fell young timber for the crown, and the sawmills of Kilinti hum in the autumn. The Moot has marked the groves that may not be touched.

focuses.name: No Axe in the Old Wood
focuses.desc: Kilinti petitions the crown to remove the oldest groves from the timber contracts for good. The Golden Court, which wants the oldest trees, will not be pleased.

focuses.name: Scholars Among the Trees
focuses.desc: Scholars from Selen and Parim visit Kilinti, to sit at the roots and listen. The ents teach them one thing a year, and that only when asked.

focuses.name: Wardens of the Concord
focuses.desc: Kilinti offers the Concord a company of forest-wardens, to serve on its frontier. The Golden King accepts, and the ents do not say what they think of it.

focuses.name: The Woods Awake
focuses.desc: The Great Moot has met, and the answer is short. The groves are awake, and everything that threatens them will find the forest less patient than it was.

focuses.name: Refuge in the Trees
focuses.desc: Villagers from the burning lands flee into the forest, and the ents let them pass. The woods have always been a refuge, and are one again.

focuses.name: The Groves March
focuses.desc: The groves rise in the night, root from soil, and walk to the border. The sound is like a long slow wind, and the enemy hears it before they see it.

focuses.name: Against the Deathless
focuses.desc: The ents stand against the host that does not die. Roots crush and branches strike, and when the dead rise again, the ents are still there.

effects.tooltip: Root and branch break the dead; they do not end them.

focuses.name: The Heir's Woodsmen
focuses.desc: The forest peoples go to the Heir with their bows and their axes. The ents do not go, but they make it known that the roads through Kilinti are open to him.

focuses.name: The Forest Heals
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the forest begins to close its wounds. Saplings spring up where the burning was, and the ents walk slowly home.
